findings.reason: without a bound fixed before the run, §3's pacing measure is unfalsifiable and the one property that keeps the read-only client from being rate-limited or blocked is unverified.
findings.text: §3's done-when requires the measured request rate to stay "at or below the stated bound", but the only rate figure in the plan surfaces after the fact in a build comment (1.818 requests/s "below 2"); as written the same worker states the bound and measures against it, so the pacer guard can never show a refusal and a client with no pacing at all still passes by declaring a bound above its own measured rate

findings.reason: the heading is what a dispatch brief takes as the node's goal, and as written it carries the wrong host and an unconditional fetch the section has not established.
findings.text: the §4 heading "A document file is fetched from IDM by identity and version" names IDM as the file source and asserts a fetch, while the section body and the `document-source` decision ("production-read-only") read the file through production ICP under the same guardrails, and §4's own evidence says no file has ever been fetched from either instance; a node composed from the heading would be pointed at the IDM host with a deliverable the section itself allows to close as "no route exists"

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — both evidence anchors (`docs/evidence/fragments/icp-api-access/icp-read-only-client.html#icp-read-only-client-evidence` and `...#icp-plant-structure-and-component-reads-evidence`) exist in their cited files, the section hrefs (`icp-api-access#s2`) resolve to real section ids, and the blocking plan's references to this plan resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §3's done-when compares the measured request rate against "the stated bound", but the plan never states a bound, so the gate can be satisfied by any rate.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every receipt the comments cite sits under `docs/evidence/fragments/icp-api-access/`, and fetched content is required to stay in the private cache outside the plan's and the repository's tree.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan, stage, ticket or version identifiers are carried into the quantities or rules the sections impose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §4's heading states the file is fetched from IDM while the section's own body and the `document-source` decision read it from production ICP, so heading and body disagree about which host the section reads.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of §2, §3 and §4 names one deliverable; §4's two closure branches answer a single question (whether production exposes a document-file read) and each branch is separately checkable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — both declared section dependencies resolve (`s3` and `s4` on `icp-api-access#s2`, which exists), and `plan-blocks iter-signal-context-and-enrichment` is matched by that plan's `s4` declaring `icp-api-access#s3` and `icp-api-access#s4`.
